answers.answer: Build three shuffled tiers and stack them top to bottom: 1 randomly dealt Conflict I card, then 5 randomly dealt Conflict II cards, then all 4 Conflict III cards in shuffled order. Return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘three separately shuffled tiers’; final order ‘1 card’ from I, ‘5 cards’ from II, and ‘all 4’ III; unused cards returned without looking.

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and the third Agent (Swordmaster) beside the board. Each has 12 troops total: 3 in their garrison and 9 in supply. Each starts with 1 water, one cube at the bottom of each of the four Faction Influence tracks, and 0 VP in a three-player game or 1 VP in a four-player game.
answers.evidence: Setup: 2 Agents on Leader, third Agent set aside; 12 troops, 3 in garrison; 1 water; one cube on each Faction’s bottom space; Score track at 1 in 4-player, otherwise 0.

answers.answer: Yes. Agent turns are optional, so you may take your Reveal turn while Agents remain. After taking a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue cards may be played during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns, so you may still play one during the Reveal turn, but not on a later turn after it.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘Agent turns are optional’ and after Reveal ‘your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.’ Plot cards may be played during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up and use one matching Agent icon to send exactly one Agent to an unoccupied board space. A card with no Agent icon cannot be used for an Agent turn. Pay the space’s costs and meet its requirements before resolving any space or card effects; if you cannot pay, you cannot send the Agent there. You cannot use one card to send multiple Agents.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: play one card; choose only one Agent icon; one card cannot send multiple Agents; space must be unoccupied; pay costs and meet requirements immediately before resolving effects.

answers.answer: No. The entry cost must be paid before resolving effects from the played card or the space, so the card’s spice gain cannot pay Conspire’s 4-spice cost when you have only 3. After paying the entry cost, resolve the board-space effect, the card’s Agent box, and the one-space Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: ‘Costs are paid immediately, before resolving any effects of the space or the played card’; effects then resolve ‘in any order’ after entry cost.

answers.answer: You can deploy all 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 of the 4 already in your garrison, for a maximum of 5 troops. Recruited troops not deployed go to your garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its four recruits go to your garrison and cannot normally be deployed there.
answers.evidence: Deploying: at a Combat space, deploy any or all troops recruited this turn plus up to two more from your garrison. Board-space entry lists Rally Troops as ‘not a Combat space’ and its recruits go to garrison.

answers.answer: In order: (1) reveal all remaining hand cards, keeping them separate from cards played on Agent turns; (2) resolve the Reveal boxes of the newly revealed cards, in any order; (3) set Combat strength; (4) clean up. Reveal boxes on cards already played on Agent turns are not used. At cleanup, put all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn four steps: Reveal Cards, Resolve Reveal Effects, Set Strength, Clean Up; effects are from cards ‘you just revealed (not of cards played during Agent turns earlier this round).’

answers.answer: Yes, you may buy a card’s replacement if you can afford it, because the Imperium Row is refilled immediately after a purchase. Persuasion from multiple sources may be pooled for one card, and Persuasion from one source may be split across cards. Unspent Persuasion is lost at the end of the Reveal turn. Acquired cards go to your discard pile and are not used immediately. A card’s Acquire effect resolves once at the moment you acquire it.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: may pool or split Persuasion; cannot save it; row refills immediately; acquired cards go to discard and ‘you don’t use them right away’; Acquire box effect happens ‘at the moment you acquire the card.’

answers.answer: The strength is 10: 3 troops are worth 6 and 4 revealed swords are worth 4. If your last troop is removed, strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased by any means, including swords. For a value over 20, flip the Combat marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Set Strength: each Conflict troop = 2; each revealed sword = 1; no troops means 0 and cannot be increased; over 20, flip marker to +20 and start again.

answers.answer: During Combat, each player with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass, beginning with the First Player and proceeding clockwise. A pass does not prevent playing on a later turn. Combat resolves once all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. A ‘when you win a Conflict’ card is played only after you have won and before the next phase; it cannot trigger on a first-place tie because nobody wins.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: players with at least one troop may play or pass in First Player order; ‘not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; resolve after consecutive passes; win-trigger cards played after winning before next phase.

answers.answer: If A and B tie for first, nobody wins; A and B each receive the second reward. C and D still compete for the third reward, so C gets it and D gets none. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, even in two- or three-player games. A tie for third gives nothing, and a player with 0 strength receives no reward. After rewards, all Conflict troops go to their owners’ supplies, not their garrisons.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first means no winner and each gets second; in a 4-player first-place tie, the other two compete for third. Tied second each gets third; tied third gets nothing; 0 strength no reward; troops return to supply.

answers.answer: Normal harvesting happens when an Agent is sent to a Maker space: Imperial Basin gives 1 base spice, Hagga Basin 2, and The Great Flat 3, plus any bonus spice there. In Phase 4: Makers, check The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, and Imperial Basin; add 1 bonus spice from the bank to each space with no Agent on it. If an Agent moved away and the space is empty in Phase 4, it does accumulate bonus spice.
answers.evidence: Board spaces list spice and costs; FAQ gives base spice as Imperial Basin 1, Hagga Basin 2, Great Flat 3. Makers phase adds spice to empty spaces; ruling says a space vacated before Phase 4 accumulates it if still empty.

answers.answer: Reaching 10 VP mid-round does not end the game immediately: the trigger is checked at the end of the round in Phase 5: Recall. The game also ends at that check if the Conflict Deck is empty, including after the last Conflict was revealed. Before determining the winner, players may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards. Tiebreak order is spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Scoring: trigger at the end of a round if a player has 10+ VP or Conflict Deck is empty; Endgame Intrigue resolves first; tie sequence ends with most recent Reveal turn.

answers.answer: The VP from reaching 2 Influence is lost if you drop below 2 and regained if you reach 2 again. The bonus earned at 4 Influence is kept if you later drop below 4, and can be earned again by dropping back and advancing again. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance and its VP; tying the holder does not take it, while rising above the holder transfers it and its VP.
answers.evidence: Influence ruling: 2 Influence VP is lost below 2 and regained at 2; 4 Influence bonus is not given back and can be earned again. Alliance rule: first to 4 takes it; mere tie does not transfer; rising higher does.

answers.answer: When you lose 1 Influence after being tied at 5, a previously tied opponent takes the Alliance; if several were tied, you choose which one. If instead you were the only player at 4 and fall to 3, you lose the Alliance; with no other player at 4 or more to take it, it returns to the board and you lose its VP.
answers.evidence: Alliance rule: if holder loses Influence while previously tied, the previously tied player takes it, and if several were tied the holder chooses one; falling to 3 or less returns it if no player has 4+.

answers.answer: A discard instruction normally applies to a card in your hand and sends it to your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from your hand, discard pile, or in play to the game box; a Reserve card goes back to its Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or the card directs you to trash itself. You cannot reshuffle early just to inspect the top card of an empty deck; reshuffling occurs when you are unable to draw.
answers.evidence: Trashing cards: discard means hand unless specified and goes to discard pile; trash from hand/discard/in play; Reserve cards return to stack; optional except cost/self-trash. Deck exhaustion: reshuffle when unable to draw; cannot reshuffle early to look at top card.

answers.answer: Winning a Conflict for Arrakeen, Carthag, or Imperial Basin lets you place your Control marker on that space’s flag, replacing an opponent’s marker. While controlled, you receive the space’s bonus whenever any player visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Carthag, or 1 spice at Imperial Basin. If a Conflict for a space you already control is revealed, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict as a defensive bonus.
answers.evidence: Control: winning the named Conflict places/replaces the marker; owner receives bonus on any player’s visit; when a matching Conflict is revealed, owner may deploy one troop from supply.

answers.answer: For House Hagal setup, use an unused color, put one cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks, and place its remaining cubes in supply with no troops in its garrison. Remove the three Arrakeen cards marked 1P, shuffle the remaining House Hagal cards, and place that deck and its three Agents near its supply. It takes one Agent turn after each First Player Agent turn if it has an Agent in supply, not after the other human’s turns or a Reveal turn; it never Reveals. It does not collect resources, build an Imperium deck, earn Conflict rewards or VP, or claim Control, but it can take and hold Alliances.
answers.evidence: House Hagal setup and Agent turns: unused color, cubes at track bottoms, no garrison troops, remove 1P cards, remaining deck, three Agents; acts after First Player Agent turns only, never Reveals; no resources/VP/rewards/control but can hold Alliances.

answers.answer: For an occupied indicated space, keep revealing cards until an eligible unoccupied space appears. If the deck is empty or a Reshuffle card appears, immediately reshuffle and continue revealing. Ignore normal space costs, requirements, and effects; resolve only the card’s icons and instructions. Troop icons recruit from House Hagal’s supply: deploy troops if it is a Combat space, otherwise put them in its garrison. Whenever it sends an Agent to a Combat space, it may also deploy up to two garrison troops, even if that card recruited none. Harvest Spice follows its instructions; harvested bonus spice is removed from that space and returned to the bank. If a two-space card’s condition-matching option is occupied, draw a new card and do not switch to the other option.
answers.evidence: House Hagal: reveal until unoccupied; reshuffle if empty or Reshuffle appears; ignore space costs/requirements/effects; recruit/deploy as described; Harvest Spice removes bonus; for two-space card use only matching option and draw again if occupied.

answers.answer: At the start of Combat, if House Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict, reveal a House Hagal card; if it is Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Count only its sword icons and add them to 2 strength per deployed troop; humans then may play Combat Intrigue cards. House Hagal occupies its rank but receives no reward. If it wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove that human’s Control marker. Ordinary third place pays nothing, but tied humans in second each receive the third reward even in two-player play.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Combat procedure: reveal/reveal again after Reshuffle; only swords count, added to 2 per deployed troop; humans play Intrigue after. It gets no reward but occupies rank; a win removes opposing Control; tie for second pays third reward even in two- and three-player games.
